calls.head: Penalties could cost the Sharks
calls.body: The Sharks’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Maple Leafs’ power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Sharks tonight.

calls.head: The Maple Leafs better keep their heads up
calls.body: The Sharks hit a lot, but the Maple Leafs mostly don’t. San Jose is one of the league’s best for physicality, and Toronto is near the bottom. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Sharks.

surprises.head: Sergei Bobrovsky stole one
surprises.body: Bobrovsky allowed 1 goal on 31 shots, worth 3.7 expected goals: 2.7 fewer than expected. That is more than Toronto’s winning margin, not counting empty-net goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 40 starts.

surprises.head: San Jose hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: San Jose is one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 70 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 119 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Bobrovsky stands on his head
paras: Vinni Lettieri played his first NHL game since Apr 15, 2025. Mason Marchment struck first for the Sharks late in the first, but they didn’t score again. Auston Matthews tied it up for Toronto on the power play with 12 seconds left in the second. Gavin McKenna put the Maple Leafs ahead for good on the power play early in the third. Nick Paul sealed it into the empty net with 40 seconds left. Matthews finished with a goal and two assists.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Sergei Bobrovsky made 30 saves for the Maple Leafs, and Yaroslav Askarov, who gave up five goals against Boston in his last start, stopped 29 of 31.

The Maple Leafs killed all four Sharks power plays. The Sharks killed off a two-man advantage that lasted just over a minute late in the first. The Leafs improved to 4-4-2, and the Sharks fell to 4-4-1.

items.text: The Maple Leafs won for the first time in four games.
William Nylander extended his point streak against San Jose to seven games.
One of the preview’s two calls held.
